'''Joshua Kwame Awuah Oduro''' (born October 14, 2000)<ref name="GMasonBio">{{cite web|title=Josh Oduro – 2022-23 Men's Basketball Roster|url=https://gomason.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/josh-oduro/6961|website=GoMason.com|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Josh Oduro – College Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/josh-oduro-1.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Melbourne United]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason Patriots]] and the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]].

==High school career==
Oduro began attending [[Battlefield High School|Battlefield]] in [[Haymarket, Virginia]] where he played two seasons and later transferred to [[Paul VI Catholic High School|Paul VI]] in [[Chantilly, Virginia]] where he led the Panthers to a 33–4 record, a VISAA Division I state title and a No. 14 national ranking in USA Today's Top-25 poll. He was named Second Team All-Conference.<ref name="GMasonBio" /><ref name="ProvidenceBio">{{cite web|title=Josh Oduro – 2023-24 Men's Basketball Roster|url=https://friars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/josh-oduro/9391|website=Friars.com|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Oduro played four years at [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] and then transferred to [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] in his last year. With the Friars, he ranked in 10th place in the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] in scoring (15.9), seventh in blocks (1.3), fifth in field goal percentage (.527), seventh in free-throw percentage (.819), fifth in defensive rebounds (5.2), sixth in rebounding (7.5) and ninth in offensive rebounds (2.3). He also registered five double-doubles and nine games with 20 or more points, including a season-high 32-point effort against [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].<ref name="ProvidenceBio" /><ref name="2024SLNOP">{{cite web|title=Former Friar Josh Oduro To Play On New Orleans Pelicans NBA Summer League Team|url=https://friars.com/news/2024/6/28/mens-basketball-former-friar-josh-oduro-to-play-on-new-orleans-pelicans-nba-summer-league-team.aspx|website=Friars.com|date=June 28, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref>

In five seasons, Oduro scored 1,913 points, averaging 12.9; grabbed 976 rebounds, averaging 6.6 and shot 52.7 percent from the field.<ref name="ProvidenceBio" /><ref name="2024SLNOP" />

==Professional career==
===Birmingham Squadron (2024–2026)===
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Oduro joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]<ref name="2024SLNOP" /><ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans announce NBA 2K25 2024 Summer League roster presented by TripADeal|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/2024-nba-summer-league-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-tripadeal|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref> and on October 11, 2024, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans announce roster moves|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/elfrid-payton-josh-oduro-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-october-11-2024|website=NBA.com|date=October 11, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived five days later<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans waive four players|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-roster-update-four-players-waived-2024-2025-nba-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> and on October 28, he joined the [[Birmingham Squadron]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref>
===New Orleans Pelicans (2026)===
On March 4, 2026, Oduro signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pelicans.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans Sign Josh Oduro to Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-josh-oduro-to-two-way-contract|access-date=March 8, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}}</ref>
===Melbourne United (2026–present)===
On July 28, 2026, Oduro signed with [[Melbourne United]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2026–27 NBL season|2026–27 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=BREAKING: United sign NBA big man as first import |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/melbourne-united-sign-josh-oduro-as-first-import |access-date=28 July 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=28 July 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Oduro was born to Kofi and Kris Oduro.<ref name=cristodero>{{cite web |last1=Cristodero |first1=Damian |title=Basketball star Josh Oduro puts hard work on display |url=https://www.gmu.edu/news/2022-03/basketball-star-josh-oduro-puts-hard-work-display |website=George Mason University |access-date=August 9, 2026 |date=March 7, 2022}}</ref> His father ran track and played soccer in his native Ghana.<ref name=cristodero/>

Oduro and his wife, Caroline, had their first child in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brennan |first1=Sean |title=Josh Oduro is Blossoming as a Scorer and a Father |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2024/3/1/mens-basketball-josh-oduro-is-blossoming-as-a-scorer-and-a-father.aspx |website=Big East Conference |access-date=August 9, 2026 |date=March 1, 2024}}</ref>
